data.title: Form
data.tagline: Collect several fields and submit them as one task
data.description: A form organizes multiple inputs into a task such as creating an account or placing an order. It needs clear labels, validation, error placement, submission state, and a final result so people know what to fix and whether their data was saved.

distinctions.label: Fieldset
distinctions.explanation: A Form collects and submits a complete task. A fieldset only groups related fields inside a form and commonly uses a legend to name the group.

use: Any task that submits several related fields
avoid: Ask for information that is not needed for the task
Clear every field after one error
Show only a generic error at the top
Allow repeated submission while the first request is running

lessonPractice.title: A sign-up page collects an email, verification code, and password to create one account. How should the form be organized?

options.label: Put a Save button beside each field and submit all three separately
options.feedback: The fields belong to one sign-up task. Separate submissions create incomplete states and make it unclear when the account exists.

options.label: Group the fields in one form, show errors nearby, and submit them together
options.feedback: The fields complete one task, so one submission can validate them together and report whether account creation succeeded.

options.label: Submit them together but only show an 'Invalid information' message at the top
options.feedback: One submission is appropriate, but a generic message does not identify which field needs correction.

data.agentPrompt: Turn email, verification code, and password into one sign-up form submission. Show errors beside the relevant fields, prevent duplicate submission while pending, and report success or failure. Verify empty, invalid, and successful cases.
